artboards.title: A week, and trucks and rooms
New calendar: how should it work?

annotations.text:
HandsFreeOS Milestone 5: the Calendar. Same look as Milestones 1 to 4. There are no calendar types. Every calendar is the same thing, and its settings make it work like Personal, Round Robin, Service, Group/Class, Event, Resource, Collective or Dispatch, or any mix. Presets only fill in settings, labels are worked out from the settings, clashes come with a Fix button, and the booking link never changes.
Try: Main (click an appointment; turn calendars and people on and off), Phone (tap a day, an appointment, then Cancel), Presets (pick a card), Builder (change how a booking picks a person, the weights and the crew size, then Fix and Save), Conflicts (Fix, Undo, Restore) and Booking (book an AC tune-up).

Sample data only: Lone Star HVAC & Roofing is a fictional client workspace of Go Biz Help. Every screen is Thursday, September 17, 10:40 AM Central Time. People, numbers and addresses are placeholders.
Phone: the bottom bar is now Home, Inbox, Pipeline, Calendar, More. Customers moves into More, and the search at the top still finds customers. The + button starts a booking.

For you to decide on this canvas:
1. The preset names and one-line descriptions (New calendar screen).
2. The reminder wording and timing: the day before at 4 PM and about 2 hours before (Texts and emails).
3. The default booking window: 4 hours to 60 days ahead.
4. Whether the booking page shows “Booking by HandsFreeOS” at the bottom.

Choices I made that the plan didn’t spell out:
• Settings gets two tabs: My calendar (everyone) and Calendars (owners and admins). Services, resources, territories and the booking site sit inside Calendars.
• Staff booking warnings cover buffers, travel and hours. A true clash with another appointment is never allowed.
• “Maria’s rooftop unit tune-up” is a service that needs Truck 2 and a crew of two.
• Customers see the tech’s first name on the booking page and in texts.
• Texts carry a short change-or-cancel link. The real signed link is longer, so we may need a short-link step.
Booking: the customer’s side, with no HandsFreeOS menus. Use Preview to jump to a step, and Theme to see dark.
